scope: Only remaining state-mutation drain/final-spawn fence plus quick comparison of the two reported Windows fixture failures. No repetition of initial five findings or100 review.

D102_1Resolution.mutationOwnership: All ownership-sensitive state mutations now enter mutate(): run-create, lease-write, run-remove, and the entire archive/write/check/unlink operation. The tracked promise includes awaited I/O rather than just a pre-I/O boolean check. Once grace ends, close sets fenced, refuses new mutations, drains every mutation already admitted, then releases the OS owner. A mutation already inside writeAtomic/unlink therefore cannot finish after a new owner acquires the store.
D102_1Resolution.lateCleanup: Background cleanup that begins after the fence cannot issue a mutation. Already-admitted cleanup completes while ownership is retained. The existing lease-ID comparison remains an additional defense, rather than being mistaken for cross-owner atomic deletion.
D102_1Resolution.finalSpawn: runChild rechecks closing||fenced after its awaited setup/hash/beforeSpawn hook and immediately before synchronous capture/spawn. CLOSING becomes a no-child terminal outcome for jobs and is handled by the signal-less version-probe path. It no longer relies only on new prepare/acquire rejection or an optional AbortSignal.
D102_1Resolution.focusedTest: E20 holds a lease-release mutation beyond close grace and verifies another executor remains STORE_BUSY until the mutation completes. It then checks ownership can transfer and tests both job and signal-less probe refusing to launch when closing begins at beforeSpawn. This directly targets the residual's two boundaries; no test was rerun by this reviewer.
D102_1Resolution.judgment: The requested mutation-drain and final-admission repair is satisfied in the fixed source. No further implementation change is requested by this bounded review.

fixtureDelta.E17: The test now waits for never-started lease cleanup/ready after the immediate cancellation verdict, then reasserts invocation0. This matches the intentionally separate verdict/cleanup lifetime instead of assuming executing0 means all file cleanup already finished.
fixtureDelta.P1: The fake fixture writes ready-n once its stop watcher exists; the process test waits for that handshake before killing the launcher. Windows/non-Linux cleanup still requests stop-all, accepting either the fixture's self-exit marker or a stopped heartbeat. This addresses the former assumption that a parent-killed child must always execute its own exit-marker code.
fixtureDelta.livenessClaimLimit: No-heartbeat for1500ms is inactivity evidence, not an OS proof of child death; a delayed or suspended process can miss heartbeats. In this test it does not clear the product lease or authorize new execution, so it is not a new product admission regression. Describe that branch as a cleanup observation and do not use it as proof that all Windows descendant processes ended. Root owns actual fixture/process cleanup verification.
fixtureDelta.executionAttribution: The previous969 Windows result of19 pass/2 fail/3 skip remains the previous run. This source review does not convert the updated assertions into a new pass; root will supply exact new execution evidence.
